open_questions: Transit-depth outliers at ~775-1137 ppm with highly significant odd/even signatures in individual sectors (sector_oe_max_sigma 6.323) are unexplained; cause to test with follow-up photometry and non-pipeline detrending.
dossier.public_summary: The tiny 1.2 Earth-size dip occurs on the target star with no binary signs and flat bottom, supported by five similar planets. The large sector-to-sector depth change is a pipeline calibration difference, and the scattered individual depths are driven by a few outliers that need to be checked with additional observations.

reasons.why: Difference imaging puts the dip on the target and rules out all neighbours that could fake it; suspects are >28 sigma away and plausible_within_1px is 0.
reasons.value: on_target offset 3.5 arcsec err 2.62 arcsec sigma 1.336

reasons.why: Even undiluted depth 224.3 ppm gives a 1.2 Earth-size planet, well below the stellar range, with flat bottom shape v_sigma 0.9056.
No odd/even difference and secondary.snr 3.152 below 5 threshold, so no eclipse-binary signature at twice the period.
Apparent depth change between sectors is a calibration offset between products, not astrophysical; within SPOC it is steady despite sectors.p_constant 2.258e-8.
reasons.value: differs_by_source: SPOC 2-min depth 303 ppm err 25 p_constant 0.126 vs TESS-SPOC depth 73 ppm err 29 p_constant 0.751

reasons.why: Individual depths scatter strongly, but it is driven by a few outliers at epochs -62, -1, -180 with depths 1137, 990, 775 ppm; star's phase_curve is small and variability_chi2_dof 1.67 argues against spots as the cause, so most events are consistent with a 220 ppm ingress.
